title: Sun Star and Person Removal: Sky/Cloud Composite, Color Grading, and Object Removal in Photoshop

date.basis: Embedded MP4 creation_time in metadata; transcript does not independently confirm exact date

summary: This editing-focused walkthrough demonstrates removing a person from a landscape shot and achieving a cohesive sky and cloud scene through iterative color grading, cloning/patching, and perspective adjustments. The presenter walks through warming the image, matching color and luminance between two shots, painting out a subject, then building and blending oversized clouds via duplication and warping. The workflow also covers selective color corrections, HDR texture refinement, and a final vignette to guide the viewer’s eye toward the sun, interleaved with cautions about common non-destructive editing pitfalls and the importance of restraint when applying dramatic adjustments.

sections.title: Initial color grading and shot matching
sections.description: The video begins with aligning the two frames by adjusting color temperature and shadows, then adds blue split toning and a sun-focused glow. A highlight-control curve is used to brighten without blowing out the sun. The presenter establishes a starting point and compares two shots side-by-side to gauge warmth and overall tonality before proceeding.

sections.title: Subject removal and layer-based compositing
sections.description: The workflow shifts to removing a person from the scene. The creator aligns and blends layers, uses clone and healing tools, and employs content-aware methods to conceal the subject. He emphasizes keeping other parts of the shot intact, notes the usefulness of re-taking the shot if possible, and mentions not to rush into tools that create extra work if not planned on separate layers.

sections.title: Sky augmentation: enlarging and integrating clouds
sections.description: Blown-out clouds are addressed with selective color adjustments, followed by creating massively enlarged clouds by duplicating and repositioning sky elements. The clouds are blended with perspective warp and careful masking, avoiding obvious seams by using the history brush for smooth transitions. The speaker also discusses additional duplication from the mountaintop to ensure clouds cover the horizon without reintroducing the mountain into the shot.

sections.title: Refinement: vignette, HDR texture, and color balance
sections.description: A sequence of refinements aimed at guiding the viewer’s eye toward the sun: a dark, cool vignette is added, color balance is adjusted (with RAW processing and optional note on whether RAW would have been used), and Auto HDR is applied to recover ice texture. Blur plus luminosity is used to soften and diffuse the composition near the sun, with careful restraint to preserve a natural transition. The artist emphasizes avoiding overdoing HDR and uses selective painting to preserve edge textures while enhancing the dramatic light gradient.
